metadata.title: Effect of school climate on fourth-grade students’ science achievement in the United Arab Emirates: Insights from the 2023 TIMSS Dataset
metadata.venue: International Journal of Educational Research Open

confounders_identified: Language of the test spoken at home
extraction.outcome_summary: The study analyzed 34,217 fourth-grade students in the UAE from TIMSS 2023 and examined how three school-climate domains related to science achievement. Pearson correlations showed that the climate domains were interrelated, and hierarchical regression indicated that science classroom environment, attitude toward science, and social/emotional safety all significantly predicted science achievement, with social and emotional safety contributing the most unique variance. Demographic variables added explanatory power, and moderation analyses showed that absenteeism consistently moderated the climate-achievement links, while number of books at home and language of the test also moderated some relationships. The authors handled missing data with expectation maximization and used the average of the five plausible values for science achievement.
